title: Bank Nifty breaks into uncharted territory as FII billions back India’s bull run - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
SBI, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Asian Paints, IndiGo and HUL among top gainers in Tuesday’s session

Bank Nifty scaled a fresh all-time high of 62,442.20 on Tuesday, pulling the broader market higher for a second consecutive session and cementing India’s status as a relative safe haven even as Wall Street’s technology stocks remained under pressure from the ongoing unwind of AI trades.

The NSE Nifty50 closed at 25,387.40, up 96.30 points or 0.38 per cent, after touching an intraday peak of 25,501.35, a level it failed to sustain. The BSE Sensex gained 427.40 points or 0.52 per cent to settle at 82,532.19. Bank Nifty closed at 62,273.25, up 697.35 points or 1.13 per cent, its strongest close on record. PNB led the banking pack with a gain of 3.74 per cent.

Aalok Shah, Director - Strategy and Research, Monarch Networth Capital, said the confluence of strong credit growth (highest in the last 15 years); solid deposit franchise - also aided by flows through FCNR (B) deposit, contained costs both operating and credit cost is driving a more sustainable returns profile for the banking sector both private and PSU players.

“Concerns around margins pressure, if any are far too limited and only for certain pockets. We see banking sector outperformance to continue as each of the above aspects continue to gain further momentum,” he said.

Meanwhile, frontline indices Sensex and Nifty maintained the momentum on Tuesday, led by banking and FMCG sectors. Today’s gains were led by SBI, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Asian Paints, IndiGo and HUL. IT stocks, however, remained under pressure, with Infosys, HCL Technologies and Tech Mahindra closing in the red.

The Nifty IT index shed 0.90 per cent, while PSU Banks and Realty surged 1.95 per cent and 1.94 per cent respectively. The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 0.25 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 0.22 per cent.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, flagged a nuance beneath the headline strength. ...”Overseas investors remained net buyers and favoured large caps, while banks led the gains. IT lagged amid the global unwinding of expensive AI trades, and mid- and small-caps were subdued.”... He added that inflation remaining above the RBI’s tolerance range has strengthened expectations of another rate hike in December, potentially limiting valuation expansion.

That macro concern found support in data released during the session. India’s wholesale inflation accelerated to 12.29 per cent year-on-year in October, up from 11.39 per cent in September, driven by a 32.84 per cent surge in fuel and power prices and a 70.8 per cent jump in crude petroleum and natural gas inflation. India’s October CPI also breached the RBI’s upper tolerance threshold. Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research at Motilal Oswal, noted that Q2FY27 earnings were strong, aggregate profit-after-tax growth for the MOFSL universe came in at 32 per cent year-on-year against an expectation of 21 per cent, but cautioned that ...”incomplete cost pass-through could weigh on downstream manufacturers’ margins in the coming quarters.”...

Foreign portfolio investors poured ₹84,290 crore into Indian equities in the first half of November alone, putting the month on course for its strongest inflows in six years. The Indian rupee strengthened to a seven-month high near 93.40 against the dollar, aided by easing crude oil prices. Brent crude slipped to around $91.56 per barrel as the International Energy Agency projected global supply to exceed demand by 1.7 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter. Ajit Mishra, SVP, Research at Religare Broking, said ...”We now see potential for the Nifty to move towards 25,700, with the immediate support base shifting higher to the 25,000–25,200 zone.”...

In a development with cross-border significance, BSE received approval from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission to offer its BANKEX Index Futures in the United States, making it the first Indian sectoral index futures contract to receive such clearance. Separately, SEBI is reportedly considering tighter rules on margin trading facility to control leverage in midcap and smallcap stocks, where margin-funded positions have risen to ₹1.53 lakh crore.

Looking ahead, Anthropic’s IPO opens on Wednesday, November 18, in what could rank among the largest global listings of 2026. Nvidia’s quarterly earnings will be closely tracked for their ripple effect on Indian IT stocks. The minutes of the US Federal Reserve’s October meeting, scheduled for release at 12:30 am IST on November 19, will provide the next major cue on the interest rate trajectory. Ankur Punj, Managing Director at Equirus Wealth, summed up the broader stance. ...”While global uncertainties and volatility remain near-term risks, India’s domestic growth outlook and improving earnings trajectory continue to support the medium-term investment case.”...
